Headline: It begins
Text: The world (or at least Wichita, Kansas) is introduced to the very first Trapper Keeper, created by E. Bryant Crutchfield.

Headline: Trapper on TV!
Text: The first Trapper Keeper commercial is aired in the test market, Wichita, Kansas

Headline: Nickelodeon & the Walkman
Text: Two '80s icons make their debut.

Headline: Rubik's Cube
Text:
Launches worldwide to frustrate the masses. 
This same year, Pacman appears in arcades everywhere.

Headline: Trapper goes Prime Time
Text:
Trapper Keeper becomes a national brand and launches its first primetime television campaign.   
Print advertisements run featuring a Kansas teacher’s glowing endorsement

Headline: A royal wedding
Text: Prince Charles Marries Lady Diana

Headline: Thriller!
Text: The same year that Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ album is released, the first CD (Billy Joel’s “52nd Street”) and CD player are commercially released on Oct. 1, in Japan.

Headline: Say hello to style
Text: In the same year that Motorola introduces the first commercial mobile cell phone. Trapper introduces the forever popular Horse and Rainbow Heart designs.

Headline: Who ya gonna call?
Text: Ghostbusters! debuts on June first. This same year, the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles made their first appearance in comic books.

Headline: Throw away Cameras?
Text: Fujifilm develops the modern disposable camera for commercial use

Headline: Back to the Future
Text: Back to the Future is released. That same year, another blast from the blast occurs when the Titanic shipwreck is found.

Headline: Television Milestones
Text: Fox TV begins regulary broadcasting and Full House debuts.

Headline: The Designer Series
Text: The Designer Series is introduced, featuring abstract designs and state-of-the-art computer-generated images. The series successfully runs through 1995!

Headline: Just Do It.
Text: Nike coins their famous tagline, the same year that CDs outsell vinyl records for the first time

Headline: Tetris Anyone?
Text: The first Game Boy is released

Headline: Technology leaps
Text: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched aboard the space shuttle Discovery and begins operations. This same year the very first web page and web browser are created.

Headline: AHHHH
Text: Home Alone hits theaters.

Headline: Be Like Mike
Text: Michael Jordan and the Chicago Bulls win their first NBA Championship. He goes on to win his 6th, and last, championship in 1998.

Headline: Shop til you drop
Text: The Mall of America opens for business.

Headline: WWW Dots and Beanie Babbies
Text: The world changes as the World Wide Web goes public (available for everyone on a royalty-free basis), and Beanie Babies make their first appearance at a toy expo

Headline: Good news. Bad news.
Text: A The good news, 1994 saw the debut of the popular TV show “Friends.” Unfortunatly it also saw a player’s strike prematurely end the Major League Baseball season & precluding the playing of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.

Headline: Ready to Rock?
Text: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame opens its doors in Cleveland, Ohio.

Headline: The rise of boy bands!
Text: Backstreet Boys release their first international album, “Backstreet Boys” and ‘NSYNC releases their first official single, “I Want You Back”

Headline: A Titanic haul
Text: The film Titanic debuts and becomes the highest grossing film of its time.

Headline: Technology advances
Text:
The first portable MP3 players start appearing in the market and the 
Furby is introduced... becoming the “must-have” toy for the holiday season.

Headline: Y2K Terror!
Text: The Y2K scare causes panic around the world that technology would crash at 12:00AM, January 1, 2000. It didn't. However something that did happen: The Breitling Orbiter 3, became the first balloon to fly around the world non-stop

Headline: A new Millennium Begins
Text: And so does Survivor. The first season airs and quickly becomes one of the most watched shows for over a decade.

Headline: Trapper on South Park
Text: South Park creates an episode about a futuristic computerized Trapper Keeper. Season 4, Episode 12, “Trapper Keeper.”

Headline: Introducing, the iPod
Text: Apple releases the first generation iPod

Headline: Record Breaking Power
Text: Barry Bonds sets a new single-year home run record in professional baseball – 73 homers!

Headline: American Idol
Text: The very first season of American Idol debuts with Kelly Clarkson becoming the first winner of the popular singing competition

Headline: Shout out from John Mayer!
Text: He calls Trapper Keepers “the genesis of OCD for my generation” on VH1’s “I Love the 80s.”

Headline: Last Punch Buggy
Text: The very last “old-style” Volkswagen Beetle rolls off the production line in Puebla, Mexico

Headline: Trapper on the Big Screen
Text: John Heder proudly uses a Trapper Keeper when he plays the title role in Napoleon Dynamite.

Headline: Getting Social
Text: Just one year after Mark Zuckerberg launches Facebook, YouTube makes its appearance online.

Headline: Trapper on Family Guy
Text: The iconic binder makes an appearance on Family Guy when Meg asks Tom Brady if he will sign her Trapper Keeper. Season 4, Episode 20, “Patriot Games.”

Headline: Game Board Official
Text: Hasbro transforms the Trapper Keeper into a game piece in their “Totally ‘80s” edition of Trivial Pursuit.

Headline: Build it your way
Text: Trapper Keeper introduces a full line of customizable products.

Headline: Harry's story ends.
Text: The 7th and final Harry Potter book is released, “Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows”

Headline: Going for Gold
Text: Michael Phelps sets the world record for most gold medals won at a single Olympic games when he takes home eight gold medals from Beijing, China.

Headline: 100 Meter Dash
Text: Usain Bolt of Jamaica sets a new World Record for the Men’s 100 Meter Dash in Berlin at 9.58 seconds

Headline: Tablet Time
Text: Tablet computers gain popularity when Apple releases the first generation iPad

Headline: Another Royal Wedding
Text: The royal wedding between Prince William and Kate Middleton takes place in the United Kingdom

Headline: Trapper on the big screen
Text: Trapper Keeper is featured on the hit film “Perks of Being a Wallflower”

Headline: An Ode to Trapper Keeper
Text: In an online article titled “An Ode to Trapper Keeper,” editor Joshua Fruhlinger dubs the Trapper Keeper the “greatest 3-ring binder ever created.”

Headline: The dream lives on.
Text: 50th anniversary of Martin Luther King Jr.’s “I Have a Dream” speech

Headline: Oh Snap. Look who's back!
Text: Trapper Keeper is re-launched, introducing a full line of products that feature the innovative Snapper Trapper™ feature to aid in quick & easy student organization

Headline: New Trapper Keeper designs!!
Text: Trapper Keeper released a new collection full of palm trees and ocean waves called Fun In The Sun™! With designs like these, it will feel like summer all year-round.

Headline: Introducing Star Wars Trapper Keepers!
Text: A new alliance entered our galaxy—Star Wars™ and Trapper Keeper®! School supplies have never been more out of this world.

Headline: Hello Kitty Trapper Keepers!
Text: Cute, trendy, and organized. See how Hello Kitty® and Trapper Keeper® make staying organized both fun and functional.
